correctness.rationale: The closed-neighborhood predicate has the correct inclusion direction when the edge is removed. Fresh enumeration of all 1,024 masks and the complete oriented cover graphs reproduced nonempty face vectors (10,45,120,200,192,75,10) and (10,45,118,188,166,59,6), 321/293/28 matching pairs and 11/7/4 critical 4-cells for the intact/deleted/relative sets. The combined matching is acyclic; the 15-edge orbit under the action on two-subsets verifies the universal quantifier. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/73c09141-2177-43bc-bb06-30c106edfef6/check_ordinal3.py (fresh enumeration; not a replay of the packaged verifier or its mod-two rank check). For each absolute matching, drop the pair with the empty simplex to leave one critical vertex in the usual nonempty face poset. Absolute discrete Morse gives the two sphere wedges. Independently of the relative CW presentation, acyclic cancellation of unit signed incidences on the relative chain complex gives free homology of rank four in degree four only. The integral exact sequence thus gives the primitive split injection. To check the 'under Y' statement directly, extend the actual inclusion Y → X to Y ∨ (four S^4) → X by based Hurewicz representatives of a complement to the image; this is an integral homology isomorphism between simply connected CW complexes, hence a homotopy equivalence by Whitehead. The simplicial inclusion is a cofibration, giving the four-sphere wedge cofiber. Neither the mod-two ranks nor merely comparing absolute wedge counts suffices for these conclusions.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical symmetric example and a single graph-edge deletion is a natural perturbation covering every edge by symmetry. The result determines which type of integral map survives the perturbation: a primitive rank-seven inclusion with four independent cofiber generators, not just the size of two homology groups. This is a usable exact reference for comparisons of the topology of dominance complexes under edge changes. No canonical basis or general fault theorem is claimed.
